simple.meaning: גָּלִיל (gâlîyl) is a Hebrew word meaning “a valve of a folding door (as turning); also a ring (as round).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: גָּלִיל (H1550) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 6:34, with occurrences in 1 Kings, Esther, Song of Solomon.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּלִיל (H1550) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in גָּלִיל (H1550) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: גָּלִיל (gâlîyl) / H1550 is traced through 1 Kings 6:34, Esther 1:6, Song of Songs 5:14 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a valve of a folding door (as turning); also a ring (as round)
definitions.full: H1550. galil I. [ גָּלִיל ] adjective turning, folding (= revolving), plural גְּלִילִים of leaves of doors 1Kin 6:34 (twice in verse).

occurrences.englishText: and two doors of cypress wood. The two leaves of the one door were folding, and the two leaves of the other door were folding.
